sources.finding: RAE derives torrar from Latin torrere, to toast; its present subjunctive and usted imperative include exactly torre. This is a conventional verb reading with a different lexical history from noun torre < turris. No shared tower component or relative sense frequency is proved.
Treccani records torre as a popular/poetic contracted infinitive of togliere.
Treccani derives togliere/tollere/torre from Latin tollere, distinct from tower turris. Rarity or literary register cannot remove a documented homonym.

Treccani independently lists anicino as derived from anice: an anise-seed biscuit. This supports the finite anic- derivational boundary in anicino, not a universal s/c correspondence or an unlisted corpus membership.

decisions: Withdraw both unsplit torre admissions before any remote publication. Preserve anis six IDs. Turr canonical stays research-only; all seven tower core IDs have individual blockers. Save anic as a separately typed research-only finite derivational branch without inventing a corpus ID.
